hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: A node is 'Root' if its parent pointer P is null.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: A node is 'Leaf' if it has a non-null parent and never appears as a parent P for any child node.

hints.title: Query Construction
hints.text: Otherwise, it is 'Inner'. Left join the table on t1.N = t2.P to detect child presence.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT DISTINCT
    t1.N AS N,
    IF(t1.P IS NULL, 'Root', IF(t2.P IS NULL, 'Leaf', 'Inner')) AS Type
FROM Tree AS t1
LEFT JOIN Tree AS t2 ON t1.N = t2.P
ORDER BY 1;
```

variables: N: number of nodes in binary tree
complexity.notes: Left join to check child presence followed by classification and sort.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per row take quadratic time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for child presence lookup.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Identify parent nullness for root and absence in parent column for leaves.

solutions.approach: Left Join Child Detection and Conditional Classification
solutions.code:
SELECT DISTINCT
    t1.N AS N,
    IF(t1.P IS NULL, 'Root', IF(t2.P IS NULL, 'Leaf', 'Inner')) AS Type
FROM Tree AS t1
LEFT JOIN Tree AS t2 ON t1.N = t2.P

solutions.approach: Left Join Child Detection and Conditional Classification
solutions.code:
SELECT DISTINCT
    t1.N AS N,
    CASE 
        WHEN t1.P IS NULL THEN 'Root'
        WHEN t2.P IS NULL THEN 'Leaf'
        ELSE 'Inner'
    END AS Type
FROM Tree AS t1
LEFT JOIN Tree AS t2 ON t1.N = t2.P
ORDER BY 1;
